history.notes:
PASS: all 12 rubric items in plan section 7 hold. I reviewed git diff a6a4f68..63477e3 in full.

CORRECTNESS. The library change in _empty_stretches only removes the base-branch exemption, so chords are paired in stable order on every branch. I also checked the maths. The base f(sigma) lies on the boundary of f(H), and f(b) leaves the stable line transversally at x_0 and x_m. So the gaps just outside the base are outside f(H), and an even number of interior crossings lies on each side of the base. Pairing every interior crossing in stable order therefore never pairs across the base, so the new rule is consistent with clause (b) of the reading. The 'outermost crossing stays unpaired' claim for odd counts is correct for zip over a stable-sorted list. No CLAUDE.md invariant is touched.

PER ITEM:
(1) Met. I ran the branch suite myself: 1211 passed, 47 skipped, 5 deselected, 1 xfailed (only C3, no XPASS), in 207 s.
(2) Met on the test engineer's evidence: base 1200 passed, 2 xfailed. The collected-id diff is +11 with none removed, and the counts reconcile.
(3) Met. Exactly the seven planned files, 261+/99-. Nothing under docs/, .refactor/, CLAUDE.md or artifacts/.
(4) Met on the test engineer's asserting check.py over 63 items. The only differences are on k32_series 2-10 and match plan section 5 exactly, including the one token v_4 -> v_3.
(5) Met. The grep is empty. Four old lines are touched (4 removed, 2 added). The extra removal is the dead (base_branch,) = ends, which the plan allowed removing once unused. The plan's own sketch is already 5 lines counting + and - together, so 'at most 4' must count touched lines, and this change is shorter than that sketch.
(6) Met. p1_tested is [0,0,0,2,3,4,9,13,13,13,13] on both sides, with 0 disagreements on the branch.
(7) Met. chords_checked is at least 1 on every k32 step 2-10; 36 series readings + 11 build readings = 47, the analyst's count. On base the test fails on k32 only. Clause (d) fires at steps 2-10, not 8-10 as predicted, because the chain chord (11,12) spans three gaps from step 2 on. That is the plan's own clause catching a wrong chord the prediction overlooked: stricter, not a defect.
(8) Met. checked = 1 on k10, inversion, inversion_period2 and heteroclinic. p3_6_blasts takes a visible skip, after first asserting not checked.
(9) Met. Base gives (9,10),(11,12); the branch gives (11,10),(9,12).
(10) Met. Call sites and _incomplete_footprints code are unchanged. One docstring word changed ('last' -> 'outermost', PartitionFamily.py:1018): it is in a listed file, accurate under the new rule, and not a scope breach.
(11) Met. I re-ran the greps: 'chain order' appears only in the History line :91, and the test file has none.
(12) Met. The printed k28_two_blasts rows match the restated example.

MY SPOT CHECKS. Besides the full suite, I made a deliberate break of my own, different from the test engineer's A/B/C. I replaced zip(on_branch[::2], on_branch[1::2]) with zip(on_branch[::2], on_branch[1::2][::-1]); on k32's 11,10,9,12 this rebuilds the old chain chords (11,12),(9,10). Eight tests went red: both unit pins, the series base-chord test [k32_series], T [k32_series], and the foreign test on all four of its cases. 19 passed. The file was restored with git checkout, and both worktrees are clean.

THE OTHER REVIEW POINTS (none affect the grade):
- The diff is 360 lines against the ~200 estimate, because of the 133-line helper and the docstrings. The estimate is not a rubric item.
- Removing the toothless tie assertion (12,'chord') in empty[11] was plan-directed and verified toothless: all cdists are 1.0 and the sort is stable.
- base_chord_misreadings reads only computed polylines (arc_polyline, root/tail nodes, crossing coords) and never calls the map. Each gap is closed at the crossings' own coordinates and read at its arc-length midpoint, so gaps with 0-2 nodes are handled. In the anchor-cornered lobe a zero-length gap before the anchor is skipped, and (b) treats the first gap as the base. The SimpleNamespace(trellis, hole_bridge_ids=[hb]) call relies only on the two attributes the kernel reads, the same harness as test_iterated_cut.py. One caveat: a chord coinciding with another hole's stretch keeps kind 'hole' through setdefault, so (d) skips it. That is harmless (it is empty anyway), and the test engineer's teeth note covers it.
- The functools.cache in test_foreign_chords.py now keeps the p3_15/p3_16/heteroclinic/p3_6_blasts builds alive for the whole run, where the old module-scoped fixture released them after the module. Fine at the current suite memory; worth knowing.

HOUSE STYLE AND DOCSTRINGS:
- The docstrings are good. There is one rule ('stable order on every branch'). The k=2.8 example uses current ids. The History is one condensed chain. No chain-order claim and no known-issue claim on T remain.
- Minor nits, which do not affect the grade:
  - The misread closure is redefined inside the loop.
  - gaps = {} has no annotation.
  - Gap keys mix 'anchor'/'tail' strings with int ids.
  - _lobe_image keeps its untyped parameters (moved verbatim).
  - The helper imports the private _hole_stretches (the helpers already import private kernels).
  - _incomplete_footprints' log and describe() text still say 'last', which is slightly inconsistent with its docstring's 'outermost'.
  - The CLAUDE.md 'Partition families' bullet still says chain order (planned for B12).
